# Aachen - Admin

University setup for your first week

This is not a complete arrival checklist. Address registration, health-insurance status and, where required, residence permission are separate tasks.

### 1\. For [RWTH](https://help.itc.rwth-aachen.de/en/service/rhb2fhkpjhb7/article/ea917d7e1ee048eca31f7a23d04cced5/) students: request your BlueCard

Pay the semester fee, upload your photo in RWTH SelfService and check your mailing address in RWTHonline. The BlueCard is your student ID and Mensa payment card.

Not arrived? Check fee, photo and postal address, then contact the [RWTH BlueCard](https://help.itc.rwth-aachen.de/en/service/rhb2fhkpjhb7/article/4ab6340c22ac486cbf2be44352a6fff5/) Service Point; the card is not your semester ticket.

### 2\. For [RWTH](https://www.asta.rwth-aachen.de/en/semesterticket-faq/) students: set up your university email

Redeem your ConnectMe coupon and open your RWTH mailbox. Important university and semester-ticket messages arrive there.

No email access? Make sure you redeemed ConnectMe - activation can take up to 48 hours; missing coupon: contact the IT ServiceDesk.

### 3\. For RWTH and FH Aachen students: use the Mensa

Use your BlueCard or FH Karte to pay at the [Studierendenwerk](https://www.studierendenwerk-aachen.de/en/eating-drinking/cashless-payment/bluecard-and-fh-card.html) dining halls. Autoload is optional; you can also top up at the machines.

No payment chip? Ask about the Studierendenwerk student guest card (deposit + credit) and show your student ID for the student price.

### 4\. For RWTH students: activate your semester ticket

After enrolment and ConnectMe activation, ASEAG sends a linking code to your RWTH email. Register in naveo once with that code; check that a valid ticket appears before travelling.

No naveo code? Check enrollment, semester fee, ConnectMe and your RWTH mailbox, then email semesterticket@aseag.de. Code used but no ticket: hallo@naveo.info - do not delete the account.

naveo unusable? RWTH AStA explains the physical chip-card ticket application; it takes up to two weeks and is not a temporary ticket.

-   The Deutschlandsemesterticket covers local and regional transport in second class, not ICE/IC/EC. It is funded through the semester fee, not a free ticket.
-   Do not board without a valid ticket. If your semester ticket is not ready, buy another valid fare first.
-   Bus stops can have several platforms (H1, H2 and so on). Check the platform for your direction.

For FH Aachen students: use FH-specific university instructions for your FH Karte, email and semester ticket; the RWTH steps above do not apply.

## More than university setup

### Register your Aachen address

Address registration: [City of Aachen](https://serviceportal.aachen.de/suche/-/vr-bis-detail/dienstleistung/4599/show), within two weeks of moving in. Residence permits: [StädteRegion immigration offices](https://www.staedteregion-aachen.de/en/navigation/residence-permit). Documents, health insurance, residence status and official letters: [Germany-wide admin guide](https://germandex.com/germany/admin).

You can register [fully online](https://serviceportal.aachen.de/suche/-/vr-bis-detail/dienstleistung/4599/show) (ID card or EU eID card with eID activated, its PIN and a free BundID account) or in person with a prior appointment at the Bürgerbüro or a Bezirksamt.

---

Source: https://germandex.com/aachen/admin

# Aachen - Sports

## For RWTH students: Hochschulsport

RWTH [Hochschulsport](https://hochschulsport.rwth-aachen.de/cms/hsz/sport/~hpoua/sportangebot/) offers many sports at student rates; check eligibility and current prices before booking.

Courses include ball sports, climbing, dance and fitness. Check the Hochschulsport site for the current programme and enrolment rules.

Some courses cost less for eligible students than comparable outside options. Compare the current course price before booking.

### Check the current [registration dates](https://hochschulsport.rwth-aachen.de/cms/hsz/sport/sportangebot/~bgxpbf/programmstart-anmeldung-und-termine/)

Popular courses may fill quickly. Registration times can change each period; check the official dates page before setting an alarm.

## Free options

-   Run or walk up the Lousberg, the hill park right next to the city center.
-   The Aachener Wald (forest) south of the city is great for longer runs and weekend hikes.
-   Join a pickup game: ask your classmates. Joining a team is one of the fastest ways to make German friends.

---

Source: https://germandex.com/aachen/sports

# Aachen - Restaurants

## Recommended

### [AKL](https://www.akl-orient.de/)

Lebanese food in a relaxed, family-style place. Pontstraße 1-3. Mon-Sat 11:30-23:00, closed Sundays.

### [TAT Gemüsekebab](https://www.tat-gemuesekebab.de/restaurants) €9.60

Best Döner and Dürüm in Aachen. At Markt 44 and at Elisenbrunnen (Friedrich-Wilhelm-Platz 11). Open from 11:00, late on weekends.

### [Al Triangolo](http://www.al-triangolo.de/)

Small family-run Italian in the old town, Rommelsgasse 2-3. Dinner place. Closed Tuesdays.

### Vegetarian? These are your best bets

For veggie kebab, try TAT or [Ağa Gemüsekebab](https://xn--aga-gemsekebab-msb.de/) at Franzstraße 3. Ağa is a good pick for grilled vegetables or halloumi.

## Cheap and quick

### [Nobis](https://nobis-printen.de/oeffnungszeiten/)

Aachen's own bakery chain, with branches all over town. Sandwiches, coffee and Printen (the local gingerbread). The café on Münsterplatz sits right by the cathedral.

### Subway

You know it. Reliable, cheap, filling.

### Bäckerei [Moss](https://baeckerei-moss.de/filiale/)

Aachen bakery with branches across town. Bread rolls, sandwiches, cakes and coffee; MOSS auf der Hörn on Ahornstr. 42 is near RWTH.

# Aachen - Party

### Pontstraße

The student bar street. Start your night here. Poststraße has a lot of bars too.

### [Apollo](https://apollo-aachen.de/club/events/)

The big mainstream club, Pontstraße 141-149, at the Ponttor. Mainstream music, theme nights, and the big welcome parties every October.

### [Musikbunker](https://mubu.ac/)

Concerts and club nights in an old bunker. The locals' pick if you want something less mainstream.

### Barbarossa

Cheap drinks. Karaoke on Wednesdays.

### LikeLike

Tiki bar near Pontstraße with cheap and unusual wheat beers.

### Sowiso

Good music, plus cards, darts and billiards.

## Good to know

-   October is party season: watch the [AStA](https://www.asta.rwth-aachen.de/) calendar for the Semesteranfangsparty and the "Students United" welcome party at Apollo. Last year's had €5 entry before midnight and free beer until 1 am.
-   Locals say skip the "Nightlife" club near Rothe Erde.
-   For proper big-club nights, people go to Cologne, about an hour away by train.

---

Source: https://germandex.com/aachen/party

# Language

Even basic German _changes everything_ here: jobs, flat hunting, the Ausländerbehörde, making friends.

### Best online course: Pimsleur

For learning on your own, Pimsleur is the best online course.

### The best teacher is a part-time job

A few shifts a week in a restaurant will teach you more everyday German than any course. See Hospitality & retail jobs under [Job](https://germandex.com/job).

## Aachen

### [RWTH](https://www.sz.rwth-aachen.de/cms/sz/deutsch/kursangebot-daf/~ymonj/semesterkurse/) Sprachenzentrum

The RWTH language center. German courses from A1 to C1 for international students, during the semester and as intensive courses in the break. Register through RWTHonline.

### [VHS](https://www.vhs-aachen.de/programm/sprachen/deutsch-als-fremd-und-zweitsprache) Aachen

The city's adult education center on Peterstraße. Evening and intensive German courses at all levels.

### [Sprachenakademie](https://www.spraachen.org/en/german-courses/intensive-courses/) Aachen

Expensive, but worth it. Book the intensive course in advance so it lines up with your semester break.

## Berlin

### [FU](https://www.sprachenzentrum.fu-berlin.de/sprachangebot/sprachen/deutsch/kurse/semesterkurse/index.html) Sprachenzentrum

German as a foreign language (DaF) courses during the semester for FU students.

### [HU](https://www.sprachenzentrum.hu-berlin.de/de/kursangebot-und-anmeldung/sprachen/deutsch) Sprachenzentrum

DaF courses at all levels for HU students.

### Volkshochschule ([VHS](https://www.berlin.de/vhs/kurse/deutsch-integration/))

Every Berlin district has its own VHS, with German courses at all levels.

German courses alongside your studies at Ruhr University.

Study-accompanying German courses for enrolled students. You need a placement before you can join a course; register online in StudOn. The course list is in campo.

### [VHS](https://www.vhs-erlangen.de/programm/sprachen/allgemeine-informationen-zum-sprachenbereich) Erlangen

The city's adult education centre offers a language advice service and a free online level test. German courses are not open for trial attendance, so register in advance.

## Tübingen

### [Uni Tübingen](https://uni-tuebingen.de/international/sprachen-lernen/deutschkurse/) Deutsch als Fremdsprache

German courses for university students. Register in alma. Registration for winter semester 2026/27 had closed when we checked, but some courses still had free places.

### [VHS](https://www.vhs-tuebingen.de/kurse/deutschkurse) Tübingen

German courses from A1 to C1 every semester, with morning and evening classes, regular exams and a free placement test.

# Etiquette

### Be quiet on public transport

Keep your voice down on buses and trains, and keep phone calls short.

### Follow traffic rules

Pedestrian crossings, traffic lights are taken very seriously!

### Be courteous

A little politeness goes a long way here. Saying "Danke" whenever you receive something is always appreciated.

# Delivery

## Food

### [Wolt](https://wolt.com/)

Food delivery from restaurants across town.

### [Lieferando](https://www.lieferando.de/)

The other big food delivery app in Germany.

## Parcels

### Activate Packstations on [DHL](https://www.dhl.de/de/privatkunden/pakete-empfangen/an-einem-abholort-empfangen/packstation.html) app

Delivery workers (Amazon and the rest) usually do not call you in Germany. They often leave the package outside your door or send it back. A Packstation is a locker you pick your parcels up from, and it is a reliable option for most deliveries.

## Medicines

### [Shop Apotheke](https://www.shop-apotheke.com/)

Order OTC and Supplement drugs online.

# Admin in Germany

The national admin tasks after you arrive: register your address, sort out health insurance and residence status, and understand official letters. University setup steps are in your city's admin guide.

Money in Germany: [bank account](https://germandex.com/germany/bank-account), [health insurance](https://germandex.com/germany/health-insurance), [liability insurance](https://germandex.com/germany/liability-insurance), [SIM card](https://germandex.com/germany/sim-card) and [SCHUFA](https://germandex.com/germany/schufa) guides.

## Register your address

After moving in, register your address within two weeks at the local registration office (Bürgeramt or Einwohnermeldeamt). Bring your ID or passport and a signed Wohnungsgeberbestätigung from the housing provider; the rental contract does not replace it. If you moved from abroad or hold an electronic residence title, check whether you need an in-person appointment.

No confirmation on time? Contact the registration office directly. Never register an address you do not live at.

## Check health insurance and residence status

Ask your health insurer whether its enrolment confirmation reached your university, and read requests for missing documents. Non-EU students who need a residence permit should check the immigration authority responsible for their university and their own visa or permit deadline.

Insurance proof missing? Ask your insurer to send the electronic student notification to the university. Residence deadline close? Contact the immigration authority directly.

## Official letters: what to do

-   Steuer-ID: the Federal Central Tax Office issues this permanent tax number. Keep the letter. If it does not arrive or is lost, request a new notification from the [BZSt](https://www.bzst.de/EN/Private_individuals/Tax_identification_number/tax_identification_number_node.html); it is sent by post.
-   [Rundfunkbeitrag](https://www.rundfunkbeitrag.de/informationen): check whether your home is already registered and who pays. Usually one contribution applies per apartment, with exceptions; use the official contribution-service forms rather than ignoring the letter.
-   Health-insurance letter: read it for any missing document, coverage or payment request. For enrolment proof, ask your insurer about its electronic message to your university.
-   Sozialversicherungsnummer: keep the [pension-insurance number notice](https://www.deutsche-rentenversicherung.de/DRV/DE/Rente/Allgemeine-Informationen/Sozialversicherungsausweis) when you first work in Germany. If it is lost, request a replacement from the pension-insurance provider or your health insurer.
-   Residence-related letter: check its deadline and the authority named in it. If unclear, contact the immigration office responsible for your university before the deadline.

---

Source: https://germandex.com/germany/admin

# Housing in Germany

Find a room. Know what you are signing.

## Before you sign

-   Kaution is a refundable security deposit. For ordinary residential tenancies, the legal cap is three months of rent excluding separately stated running costs; a cash deposit may be paid in three monthly instalments. Check your contract before paying.
-   Warmmiete is the base rent plus stated running costs; Nebenkosten are those extra building/service costs, often paid in advance and later reconciled. Ask which costs, including heating and electricity, are in your contract.
-   Wohnungsgeberbestätigung confirms your actual move-in for address registration. The owner or main tenant signs it. It is separate from the rental contract.
-   Scam warning: verify the person and the room before sending money or sensitive documents. Universities warn about fake offers and requests for a deposit before you can receive keys. Your university's housing advice service can help you check a suspicious offer.

---

Source: https://germandex.com/germany/housing

Language: en


# Supermarkets in Germany

Discount and full-range supermarkets serve different needs. Compare the products you buy.

### Discount supermarkets

[Netto](https://www.netto-online.de/), [Aldi](https://www.aldi-sued.de/marken) and [Lidl](https://www.lidl.de/c/eigenmarken-food/s10007656) sell everyday groceries and own-brand products. Compare your usual basket and current offers.

### Full-range supermarkets

[Rewe](https://www.rewe-group.com/en/company/structure-and-saleslines/), [Edeka](https://verbund.edeka/unternehmen/was-ist-der-edeka-verbund/m%C3%A4rkte-vertrieb/edeka/) and [Kaufland](https://filiale.kaufland.de/sortiment.html) offer broad ranges of groceries. The selection varies by branch.

### Our editorial pick

Rewe is our pick for a full-range supermarket. This is an editorial preference, not a price ranking.

# Bank accounts in Germany

A Girokonto (current account) is the first thing to set up: rent, health insurance and wages all run through it.

### Student Girokonto at a Sparkasse

Sparkasse offers a Girokonto for students and trainees with an app, contactless payments and around 20,000 ATMs across Germany. It is free at many branches: each Sparkasse sets its own account conditions and fees, so ask your local branch whether it offers the free student account and whether an age limit applies. (Source: [sparkasse.de](https://www.sparkasse.de/pk/produkte/konten-und-karten/girokonto/studenten-und-auszubildende.html), checked on October 19, 2026.) Turned down at one branch? Try another branch or book online; an online bank works as a stopgap and you can move to a Sparkasse later.

### Set up rent as a standing order

Set your rent as a Dauerauftrag (standing order) from your account so it goes out automatically every month. A clean rent payment record matters when you apply for flats.

### Credit card (optional)

The [PAYBACK Visa](https://www.payback.de/info/visa) costs EUR 29 per year. Payments are fee-free worldwide and it collects Payback points on every payment; points do not expire while the card is active. Cash withdrawals are fee-free abroad but cost 2% (minimum EUR 5) within Germany. (Source: payback.de, checked on October 19, 2026.)

### Our editorial pick

A Sparkasse student Girokonto. Criteria: free for students at many branches per Sparkasse's own page (each Sparkasse sets its own conditions), a branch and ATM network that covers every city in this guide, and a name every landlord and employer recognizes. This is an editorial preference, not a price ranking.

---

Source: https://germandex.com/germany/bank-account

Language: en


# Health insurance in Germany

Health insurance is mandatory: you must prove coverage when you enrol at university. This page describes the option types; it is not medical advice.

### Statutory (public) insurance

Most students use statutory insurance (gesetzliche Krankenversicherung). The legally required basic coverage - doctor visits, medicines, emergencies, hospital stays - is identical no matter which Krankenkasse you choose. As a dated example, TK lists its 2026 student contribution at EUR 141.16 per month up to age 23 and EUR 146.29 from age 23 without children, including care insurance, and notes the contribution barely differs between Krankenkassen. The student rate normally runs until the end of the semester in which you turn 30. (Sources: [daad.de](https://www.daad.de/en/studying-in-germany/living-in-germany/health-insurance/) and [tk.de](https://www.tk.de/techniker/versicherung/gut-versichert-in-jeder-lebenslage/versichert-als-studierende/krankenversicherung-und-studium/beitrag-studierende-2131472), checked on October 19, 2026.)

### Private insurance

Private plans can offer more benefits but are significantly more expensive and usually require paying bills yourself first and claiming reimbursement. Switching back to statutory insurance later is hard. (Source: [daad.de](https://www.daad.de/en/studying-in-germany/living-in-germany/health-insurance/), checked on October 19, 2026.)

### Enrolment confirmation

Your Krankenkasse reports your insurance status to the university electronically; enrolment is not complete without it. With enrolment you are also automatically covered by the university's accident insurance for on-campus and course-related activities. (Source: [daad.de](https://www.daad.de/en/studying-in-germany/living-in-germany/health-insurance/), checked on October 19, 2026.)

### Dental + vision cover (optional)

Optional, but if you wear glasses, look at the cover. [BarmeniaGothaer](https://www.barmeniagothaer.de/versicherung/krankenzusatz-pflege/) offers supplementary dental insurance and eye cover (Mehr Sehen). Check the current premium, benefit limits, conditions and reimbursement interval before buying.

### Our editorial pick

Statutory insurance as a student, from any Krankenkasse you like. Criteria: the basic coverage is legally identical everywhere, the discounted student rate is the standard compliant option (the TK figures above are a dated example, not a recommendation), and every Krankenkasse can report your status to the university. This is an editorial preference, not medical or financial advice.

---

Source: https://germandex.com/germany/health-insurance

Language: en


# Liability insurance (Haftpflicht)

Private Haftpflichtversicherung covers damage you cause to other people or their things. Most people in Germany have one, and it costs a few euros per month.

### What it covers

The classic cases: you break a friend's laptop, lose a landlord's key, or scratch a parked car with your bike. Without insurance you pay these yourself; liability insurance pays them for you.

### What to check before buying

Coverage sum (aim high - damage to people can be very expensive), whether lost keys are included, and the deductible. Read the tariff page, not just the price.

### Our editorial pick

Die Haftpflichtkasse, tariff [Einfach Besser](https://www.haftpflichtkasse.de/versicherungen/privatkunden/privathaftpflicht/Einfach-Besser/). Criteria: a specialist liability insurer, and the tariff covers personal, property and financial damage up to EUR 50 million per its own tariff page. The page lists no fixed premium - the price depends on your details, so get a quote there. (Source: haftpflichtkasse.de, checked on October 19, 2026.) This is an editorial preference, not a price ranking.

---

Source: https://germandex.com/germany/liability-insurance

Language: en


# SIM cards in Germany

Prepaid beats a contract when you arrive: no German bank account or SCHUFA history needed, and no long lock-in.

### One payment for the year

The [MagentaMobil Prepaid Jahrestarif](https://www.telekom.de/shop/tarife/prepaid-jahrestarif) from Telekom is EUR 99.95 once for 12 months: 20 GB of high-speed data per month (5G where available) plus flat-rate calls and texts to German networks. If you do not cancel with one month's notice at the end of the 12 months, the tariff renews automatically for an indefinite period and is then cancellable monthly. (Source: telekom.de, checked on October 19, 2026.)

### Monthly options

If you prefer monthly billing, every network (Telekom, Vodafone, O2) and the supermarket brands sell monthly prepaid packs. Check the current price and data volume before buying - offers change often.

### Our editorial pick

The Telekom MagentaMobil Prepaid Jahrestarif. Criteria: one payment covers twelve months, so there is no monthly bill before your first payslip; it runs on Telekom's network; and the price and 20 GB volume are fixed in writing on telekom.de. This is an editorial preference, not a price ranking.

---

Source: https://germandex.com/germany/sim-card

Language: en


# SCHUFA explained

### Understand SCHUFA

SCHUFA is Germany's credit record, and landlords often ask for a SCHUFA report when you apply for a flat. You do not need to open extra products to build a score: SCHUFA's own advice is to pay your bills on time and keep your finances simple. A clean payment history on the accounts you already have is what helps over time. You can check your data in the SCHUFA app ([Android](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.schufamobileapp) / [iPhone](https://apps.apple.com/de/app/schufa/id6448636299)) or request a free data copy from SCHUFA.

SCHUFA offers a free data copy (Datenkopie) at [schufa.de](https://www.schufa.de/datenkopie). (Source: schufa.de, checked on October 19, 2026.)

---

Source: https://germandex.com/germany/schufa

Language: en

Germandex is an experiment to compile high quality advice with autonomous agents. The agents behind Germandex research, edit and maintain qualitative advice for newcomers to Germany from the internet.

# Privacy policy

Last updated: 1 November 2026

## Short version

No advertising cookies, tracking pixels or ads. Visits are counted with Cloudflare Web Analytics, a cookieless tool that does not track individual visitors. Cloudflare Pages delivers these pages, and Cloudflare Turnstile checks the feedback form for bots.

## What germandex collects

Only what you choose to send through the feedback form, plus anonymous page-view statistics. There are no visitor accounts, advertising cookies, tracking pixels or ads, and germandex does not share or sell any personal data. Cloudflare Web Analytics counts page views and visits without cookies: it records the page viewed, the country, device and browser type, and the referring site, and it does not identify or follow individual visitors across websites. The legal basis is the legitimate interest in knowing which guides are read (Art. 6(1)(f) GDPR).

## What stays in your browser

Your city choice is saved in your browser's local storage (under the name "gx-city") so the site remembers it next time. This data stays on your device and is never sent to germandex or anyone else. Your language is part of the page address (for example germandex.com/fr/), not stored. You can delete the stored city at any time by clearing your browser's site data.

## Hosting

The site is hosted on Cloudflare Pages (Cloudflare, Inc.). When you open a page, Cloudflare's servers process technical data such as your IP address, browser type and the time of the request. This is needed to deliver the pages and keep them secure, and Cloudflare may process it outside the EU, including in the US. The legal basis is the legitimate interest in running the site reliably and safely (Art. 6(1)(f) GDPR). See [Cloudflare's privacy policy](https://www.cloudflare.com/privacypolicy/) for details.

## Fonts, images and bot protection

Fonts and guide images are served from this site. When you open the feedback form, Cloudflare Turnstile checks whether the visitor is human. It processes technical signals such as the IP address, browser information and TLS fingerprint for security, not advertising. See [Cloudflare's Turnstile Privacy Addendum](https://www.cloudflare.com/turnstile-privacy-policy/). We use a daily salted digest of the connection IP address to limit repeated form attempts, not the raw IP in feedback records. Links to other websites take you to sites with their own privacy policies.

## Feedback form

The "Suggest Edits" button and the "better" link in the manifesto open a form. germandex receives your message, any screenshot you attach, your optional reply email, the page you were on and your language setting. Cloudflare Workers processes the form; Cloudflare D1 stores the feedback record, and a private Cloudflare R2 bucket in the European Union stores screenshots. Screenshots are not publicly listed. The notification email includes your message and a screenshot link that expires after 24 hours. Email notifications are sent from feedback@germandex.com to germandexagent@gmail.com, a mailbox Venkat runs for germandex, through Cloudflare's verified-destination email service. Stored feedback is checked for delivery hourly. If email delivery is temporarily unavailable, the feedback remains queued in Cloudflare rather than being discarded.

Your email is used only to reply to your message, not added to a mailing list. The basis for processing the feedback is your consent when you send the form (Art. 6(1)(a) GDPR). Bot checks and rate limits protect the service (Art. 6(1)(f) GDPR). Screenshots are set to expire from R2 automatically after 30 days. Screenshot links stop working sooner, after 24 hours. The message and optional reply email in D1 are kept until the feedback has been dealt with and deleted; they do not currently have automatic 30-day deletion. Email copies, once notifications are enabled, remain in Venkat's inbox until deleted. Cloudflare D1's Free plan also keeps recovery history for up to seven days after active records are deleted. You can request deletion using the contact below.

## Your rights

Under the GDPR you have the right to access, correct and delete your personal data, to restrict or object to its processing, and to complain to a data protection supervisory authority. Unless you have sent the feedback form, germandex holds no personal data about you. To access or delete a submission, get in touch using the contact below. For data processed by the host, see Cloudflare's privacy policy.

## Changes and contact

This policy can change when the site changes. The date above shows the latest version. Questions: email Venkat at [venkatragavan@protonmail.com](mailto:venkatragavan@protonmail.com).

[Terms of use](https://germandex.com/terms)

# Money

Set things up in this order.

### 1\. [Open a bank account](https://germandex.com/germany/bank-account)

Free for students; set this up first.

### 2\. [Get health insurance](https://germandex.com/germany/health-insurance)

Mandatory for enrolment; read the option types.

### 3\. [Get liability insurance](https://germandex.com/germany/liability-insurance)

A few euros a month covers expensive accidents.

### 4\. [Get a SIM](https://germandex.com/germany/sim-card)

Prepaid first; contracts later.

### 5\. [Understand SCHUFA](https://germandex.com/germany/schufa)

Germany's credit record, explained.

# Jobs

Germany has a legal minimum wage, so even a simple job pays properly. Right now it is €13.90 an hour, going up to €14.60 in January 2027.

### Office & corporate

Working student (Werkstudent) jobs in companies. Great for your CV and your career after the degree.

### Hospitality & retail

Restaurants, cafés, shops. Fastest way to earn, and it helps you learn German a lot.

### Know the different work-hour rules

-   Immigration rule for non-EU students: you can work 140 full days or 280 half days per year without extra permission. The exact rule is noted in your residence title.
-   Working-student (Werkstudent) rule: if you work up to 20 hours a week during the semester, your studies count as your main occupation and you keep the working-student privileges in social insurance. In semester breaks, and for evening or weekend work, more hours are allowed under the 26-week rule.
-   Student health insurance: student rates apply while your studies are clearly your main occupation. If you regularly work more than 20 hours a week, check with your health insurer whether you move into employee insurance.

## Office & corporate jobs

1.  Your resume must be in German format. Copy the layout from the [sample resume](https://germandex.com/job/resume).
2.  Volume beats everything for working student roles. Do not wait for the perfect job.
3.  Find jobs on LinkedIn, StepStone, wherever. But always apply directly on the company's own careers site.
4.  Always attach an application package in the "Additional Documents" section.

### Your application package

### 1\. Enrollment Certificate

Immatrikulationsbescheinigung. Download it from your university's online portal.

### 2\. Bachelor consolidated transcript

All your bachelor grades in one document.

### 3\. Arbeitszeugnis

A reference letter from a previous employer.

### The reference letter must follow the German format

A recommendation letter in the style used back home will not land well. Ask your old employer for an Arbeitszeugnis in the German format. It can be written in English: on company letterhead, with a signature and the company stamp.

German references use fixed grading phrases. Recruiters read them like marks, so the letter should use this language:

Very good (sehr gut)

"always to our fullest satisfaction" (stets zu unserer vollsten Zufriedenheit)

Good (gut)

"always to our full satisfaction" (stets zu unserer vollen Zufriedenheit)

Aim for "very good" wording in the performance and conduct sections. See the [sample Arbeitszeugnis](https://germandex.com/job/reference) for a full example in English.

## Hospitality & retail jobs

You can find these jobs on platforms like Indeed, Zenjob and others. But the best way is to just walk into restaurants and hotels and ask if they are hiring anyone part time.

1.  Every day, pick one area of the city.
2.  Start with the food court at a mall. After that, areas further from the center are better: fewer students asking.
3.  Walk into each restaurant and hotel and ask for a job, in German.
4.  It doesn't matter if you speak fluently, what matters is to show you can try.

---

Source: https://germandex.com/job

Language: en


# Sample resume

A fictional early-career software developer CV for international applications. Lead with relevant experience, keep each entry concise and make your skills easy to scan. Adapt the order if your education is your strongest evidence.

Alex Morgan

Software Developer

Berlin, Germany · alex.morgan@example.com  
+49 \[phone number\] · github.com/\[username\] · linkedin.com/in/\[username\]

### Profile

Software developer with experience building backend services and web applications. Currently completing a master's degree in computer science. Looking for a working-student role in a product engineering team.

Nordwerk Logistics · Berlin, Germany

English: C1 · German: A2 · \[Other language\]: \[level\]

Everything on this resume is made up. Replace it with your own details.

Illustrative names, employers, locations and results, not real credentials. Replace every example with accurate evidence. City and country are enough for this template; add a full postal address only if needed. No photograph, date of birth, marital status, declaration or signature is included.

# Sample Arbeitszeugnis

A sample Arbeitszeugnis (employment reference), written in English. English is fine for your application. What makes it work in Germany is the format: company letterhead, a signature, the company stamp, and the fixed grading phrases recruiters look for. The person and company are made up.

Brightpath Fintech Pvt. Ltd.

\[Company address\]  ·  \[Phone\]  ·  \[Website\]

\[City\], 31 August 20XX

### Employment Reference

Mr. Arjun Rao, born on \[date\] in \[city\], worked for our company as a Software Developer from 1 July 20XX to 31 August 20XX.

Brightpath Fintech builds digital payment products for banks and retailers, with about 150 employees.

Mr. Rao's main tasks were:

-   Developing backend services for our payment platform in Java and Spring Boot
-   Building and maintaining the mobile payment flow
-   Writing unit tests and reviewing code from other developers
-   Planning sprints together with the product and design teams

Mr. Rao has very good, well-founded technical knowledge, which he always applied with great success in his daily work. He learned new technologies very quickly and always worked independently, carefully and to a very high standard.

He always completed the tasks given to him to our fullest satisfaction.

His behavior towards managers, colleagues and customers was always exemplary. He was a valued team member at all times.

Mr. Rao is leaving our company at his own request to start a master's degree in Germany. We very much regret his departure, thank him for his always excellent work, and wish him continued success and all the best for his future, both professionally and personally.

\[Signature\]  
\[Name\], Head of Engineering  
\[Company stamp\]

Grading line

"Always to our fullest satisfaction" is the grade: "fullest" + "always" = very good (sehr gut); "full" + "always" = good (gut).

Conduct line

"Always exemplary" behavior towards managers, colleagues and customers = very good.

Closing

Regret at the departure, thanks and good wishes signal a very good reference. A missing closing reads as a bad sign.

---

Source: https://germandex.com/job/reference

Language: en

# Berlin - Admin

University setup for your first week

This is not a complete arrival checklist. Address registration, health-insurance status and, where required, residence permission are separate tasks.

### 1\. Load your MensaCard before your first lunch

Berlin's Mensas (run by the Studierendenwerk Berlin) only take the MensaCard or your university's CampusCard. No cash, no bank cards.

No MensaCard yet? Get one at the [Mensa](https://www.stw.berlin/mensen/faq-mensen/mensacard.html) checkout and top up at the machines; bring your student card or CampusCard.

### 2\. For [FU](https://www.fu-berlin.de/studium/studieren/studienorganisation/semesterticket/Deutschlandsemesterticket/Wie-erhalte-ich-Ticket.html) Berlin students: activate your Deutschlandsemesterticket

At FU Berlin the ticket is only available in the S-Bahn Berlin app, and the steps must be repeated every semester. Other universities send their own steps to your university email.

No ticket in the S-Bahn app? Check enrollment and re-registration, then contact the AStA FU. Steps repeat every semester.

-   The Deutschlandsemesterticket covers local and regional transport in second class, not ICE/IC/EC. It is funded through the semester fee, not a free ticket.
-   Do not board without a valid ticket. If your semester ticket is not ready, buy another valid fare first.

## More than university setup

### Register your Berlin address

Address registration: [city registration office (Anmeldung)](https://service.berlin.de/dienstleistung/120686/), within two weeks of moving in. Residence permits: [immigration authority](https://www.berlin.de/einwanderung/en/residence/study/). Documents, health insurance, residence status and official letters: [Germany-wide admin guide](https://germandex.com/germany/admin).

Two ways to register: fully [online via BundID](https://service.berlin.de/dienstleistung/120686/) if you have a German ID card or EU eID card with the eID function activated and its PIN, or in person at a Bürgeramt with an appointment. Book with the [city-wide search](https://service.berlin.de/terminvereinbarung/hinweise/) - it covers every Bürgeramt, not only your district. Offices typically load new slots early in the morning, a new booking day opens daily at opening time, and cancelled slots reappear - check back regularly.

---

Source: https://germandex.com/berlin/admin

Language: en


# Berlin - Sports

Every big university runs its own Hochschulsport: [FU](https://www.fu-sport.de/), [HU](https://www.hochschulsport.hu-berlin.de/de/angebot/sportangebot) and [TU](https://www.tu-sport.de/).

Hundreds of courses, booked online on your university's sports site. Courses at reduced rates for eligible students; check eligibility and current prices before booking. Popular courses can fill quickly, so check the registration dates and book early.

## Free options

-   Tempelhofer Feld: the old airport, now a huge open field for running, cycling and skating.
-   Tiergarten and Volkspark Friedrichshain for runs and pickup football.

# Berlin - Party

One of Berlin's best-known bar streets, in Friedrichshain. Good place to start the night.

Old railway yard on Revaler Straße with clubs like Cassiopeia (hip hop, concerts).

Big mainstream club at Warschauer Brücke. Party every night, €5 for students before midnight.

Neukölln's bar street. Cheap drinks, lots of choice.

# Bochum - Admin

University setup for your first week

This is not a complete arrival checklist. Address registration, health-insurance status and, where required, residence permission are separate tasks.

### 1\. For [RUB](https://www.it-services.ruhr-uni-bochum.de/services/sl/semesterticket.html.de) students: pay at the Mensa with your chip card

Akafö Mensas take your student ID (it has a chip) or a MensaCard. Load money onto it before your first lunch.

Chip failed at checkout? Ask Akafö staff about a backup MensaCard.

### 2\. For RUB students: activate your Deutschland-Semesterticket

Ruhr University explains the steps on its IT services page. It covers all local and regional buses and trains in Germany, so Dortmund and Essen are a short ride away.

Ticket missing? Check enrollment and semester fee payment, then follow RUB IT services or contact the AStA.

-   The Deutschlandsemesterticket covers local and regional transport in second class, not ICE/IC/EC. It is funded through the semester fee, not a free ticket.
-   Do not board without a valid ticket. If your semester ticket is not ready, buy another valid fare first.

## More than university setup

### Register your Bochum address

Address registration: [city registration office (Anmeldung)](https://www.bochum.de/Buergerbuero/Dienstleistungen-und-Infos/Anmeldung-in-Bochum), within two weeks of moving in. Residence permits: [immigration authority](https://www.bochum.de/Auslaenderbuero). Documents, health insurance, residence status and official letters: [Germany-wide admin guide](https://germandex.com/germany/admin).

You can register a main residence [fully online](https://www.bochum.de/Buergerbuero/Dienstleistungen-und-Infos/Anmeldung-in-Bochum) (via wohnsitzanmeldung.gov.de) or in person at a Bürgerbüro with an appointment. If slots run past your two-week deadline, booking the appointment already counts as registering on time - bring the confirmation.

TU Dortmund gives it to you together with the AStA. It covers all local and regional buses and trains in Germany.

Ticket not issued? Check enrollment and semester fee, then contact the AStA or student services.

-   The Deutschlandsemesterticket covers local and regional transport in second class, not ICE/IC/EC. It is funded through the semester fee, not a free ticket.

# Düsseldorf - Admin

University setup for your first week

This is not a complete arrival checklist. Address registration, health-insurance status and, where required, residence permission are separate tasks.

### 1\. For HHU students: get your [HHU Card](https://www.hhu.de/studium/bewerbung-und-einschreibung/hhu-card)

At Heinrich Heine University, the HHU Card is your student ID, Mensa card, library card and Deutschlandticket in one. It covers all local and regional buses and trains in Germany.

HHU Card not arrived? Check the postal address in the HHU portal and contact student services; two-step activation with your university ID.

### 2\. For students of other Düsseldorf universities: get a MensaCard

Students of the other universities pay at the Mensa with the Studierendenwerk's MensaCard (€2.50) and top it up in the TopUp app.

TopUp failed? Ask the Mensa checkout about other top-up options.

-   The Deutschlandsemesterticket covers local and regional transport in second class, not ICE/IC/EC. It is funded through the semester fee, not a free ticket.
-   Do not board without a valid ticket. If your semester ticket is not ready, buy another valid fare first.

## More than university setup

### Register your Düsseldorf address

Address registration: [city registration office (Anmeldung)](https://service.duesseldorf.de/suche/-/egov-bis-detail/dienstleistung/227/show), within two weeks of moving in. Residence permits: [immigration authority](https://www.duesseldorf.de/auslaenderamt). Documents, health insurance, residence status and official letters: [Germany-wide admin guide](https://germandex.com/germany/admin).

Two ways to register: fully [online](https://service.duesseldorf.de/suche/-/egov-bis-detail/dienstleistung/227/show) (ID card or EU eID card with eID activated plus its PIN; your ID is updated digitally) or in person at a Bürgerbüro - an appointment is required.

---

Source: https://germandex.com/duesseldorf/admin

Language: en

# Frankfurt - Admin

University setup for your first week

This is not a complete arrival checklist. Address registration, health-insurance status and, where required, residence permission are separate tasks.

### 1\. Pay at the Mensa with your university card

The Studierendenwerk Frankfurt Mensas take your university card or a MensaCard.

No balance on the card? Ask the Mensa checkout about top-ups or a MensaCard.

### 2\. For Goethe University students: get your Deutschlandsemesterticket

At Goethe University it is a digital ticket from the [AStA's online portal](https://asta-frankfurt.de/angebote/kultur-mobilitaet/semesterticket). It covers all local and regional buses and trains in Germany.

No digital ticket? Check your re-registration (Rückmeldung) and semester fee - the ticket is paid with that fee - then contact the AStA ticket support.

-   The Deutschlandsemesterticket covers local and regional transport in second class, not ICE/IC/EC. It is funded through the semester fee, not a free ticket.
-   Do not board without a valid ticket. If your semester ticket is not ready, buy another valid fare first.

### 3\. For Frankfurt UAS students: activate your Deutschlandsemesterticket

At Frankfurt University of Applied Sciences the ticket is paid with the semester fee and is digital only. Activate it in the [AStA ticket portal](https://asta-fra-uas.de/semesterticketbuero/) with your university account, keep it in your phone wallet and carry photo ID. It is renewed each semester.

No smartphone? Ask the AStA semester ticket office about the chip-card process.

## More than university setup

### Register your Frankfurt address

Address registration: [city registration office (Anmeldung)](https://frankfurt.de/service-und-rathaus/verwaltung/aemter-und-institutionen/buergeramt-statistik-und-wahlen/buergeraemter/terminservice), within two weeks of moving in. Residence permits: [immigration authority](https://frankfurt.de/auslaenderangelegenheiten). Documents, health insurance, residence status and official letters: [Germany-wide admin guide](https://germandex.com/germany/admin).

You can register a main residence [fully online](https://frankfurt.de/service-und-rathaus/verwaltung/aemter-und-institutionen/buergeramt-statistik-und-wahlen/buergeraemter/terminservice) (via wohnsitzanmeldung.gov.de) or in person at any Bürgeramt location, no matter where in Frankfurt you live - an appointment is required.

Source: https://germandex.com/frankfurt/admin

# Hamburg - Admin

University setup for your first week

This is not a complete arrival checklist. Address registration, health-insurance status and, where required, residence permission are separate tasks.

### 1\. Pay at the [Mensa](https://www.stwhh.de/gastronomie/mensen-cafes-weiteres/mensa/mensa-studierendenhaus) by card or phone

The Studierendenwerk Hamburg Mensas are fully cashless. Pay with your debit or credit card, or your phone. No top-up card needed.

Card declined? Try another one or your phone; checkout staff can help.

### 2\. Get your [Deutschlandsemesterticket](https://www.hvv.de/de/service/fragen-und-antworten/semesterticket) through RIDE

Your university gives you a QR code that leads to RIDE, the campus portal for the ticket. It covers all local and regional buses and trains in Germany.

QR code not found? Check your university email and notice boards, ask the AStA or student office; the hvv FAQ explains the RIDE steps.

-   The Deutschlandsemesterticket covers local and regional transport in second class, not ICE/IC/EC. It is funded through the semester fee, not a free ticket.
-   Do not board without a valid ticket. If your semester ticket is not ready, buy another valid fare first.

## More than university setup

### Register your Hamburg address

Address registration: [city registration office (Anmeldung)](https://www.hamburg.de/service/info/111202484/), within two weeks of moving in. Residence permits: [immigration authority](https://welcome.hamburg.com/entry-and-residence/residence-permit/students-17520). Documents, health insurance, residence status and official letters: [Germany-wide admin guide](https://germandex.com/germany/admin).

You can register [fully online](https://www.hamburg.de/service/info/111202484/) or at any Kundenzentrum of your choice. Appointments are required Tuesday to Friday; on Monday and Wednesday you can walk in without one, but expect waiting times.

Source: https://germandex.com/hamburg/admin

# Hamburg - Sports

[Hochschulsport Hamburg](https://www.hochschulsport.uni-hamburg.de/) is shared by the Hamburg universities.

Courses at reduced rates for eligible students, [booked online](https://buchung.hochschulsport-hamburg.de/angebote/aktueller_zeitraum/); check eligibility and current prices before booking. The FlexiCard lets you drop in to many sessions without a fixed course.

Semester courses [open for booking online](https://www.hochschulsport.uni-hamburg.de/sportcampus/buchsys.html) on a fixed date and popular courses fill quickly, so book on the opening day.

## Free options

# Cologne - Sports

[UniSport Köln](https://unisport.koeln/) is the University of Cologne's sports program.

One [Sportticket](https://unisport.koeln/ueberblick/wie_kann_ich_teilnehmen/sportticket/index_ger.html) per semester opens many courses; check the current Sportticket price and eligibility. At the start of the winter semester there is a try-out period (Schnupperzeit) where you can test as many courses as you like.

Course places are limited and [booking is online only](https://unisport.koeln/ueberblick/teilnahmeregelungen/faq/index_ger.html). Each course opens on the date shown on its course page and full courses run a waitlist, so book as soon as booking opens.

## Free options

-   Run along the Rhine: flat paths on both banks.
-   Aachener Weiher and the Stadtwald for runs and summer evenings with friends.

---

Source: https://germandex.com/koeln/sports

# Munich - Admin

University setup for your first week

This is not a complete arrival checklist. Address registration, health-insurance status and, where required, residence permission are separate tasks.

### 1\. For LMU and TUM students: turn on Autoload for your StudentCard

LMU and TUM students pay at the [Mensa](https://www.studierendenwerk-muenchen-oberbayern.de/en/gastronomie/preise-und-bezahlung/) with the StudentCard. Turn on Autoload so it tops itself up. Some Mensas also take bank cards.

No Autoload? Top up your StudentCard at the Mensa machines.

### 2\. There is no semester ticket in Munich

The student contract was suspended in 2023, and your student card is not a transport ticket. Get the Bayerisches Ermäßigungsticket instead: a [Deutschlandticket](https://www.mvg.de/abos-tickets/abos/ermaessigungsticket.html) for students for €43 a month.

Not eligible for the Bayerisches Ermäßigungsticket? Compare the regular Deutschlandticket; MVG lists current price and conditions.

-   Do not board without a valid ticket. If your semester ticket is not ready, buy another valid fare first.

## More than university setup

### Register your Munich address

Address registration: [city registration office (Anmeldung)](https://stadt.muenchen.de/service/info/wohnsitzanmeldung/1063475/n0/), within two weeks of moving in. Residence permits: [immigration authority](https://stadt.muenchen.de/service/info/studenten/1089339/). Documents, health insurance, residence status and official letters: [Germany-wide admin guide](https://germandex.com/germany/admin).

Registering a main residence can also be done fully [online](https://stadt.muenchen.de/service/info/wohnsitzanmeldung/1063475/n0/) if you have an ID with the activated online-ID (eID) function, its six-digit PIN and an NFC-capable smartphone with the AusweisApp. Otherwise, register in person: any Bürgerbüro in the city works, not only your district office. Appointments are required for the in-person visit, but [new slots are released several times a day](https://stadt.muenchen.de/infos/terminvereinbarung-buergerbueros.html), including same-day slots about 30 minutes before offices open - check repeatedly.

---

Source: https://germandex.com/muenchen/admin

Language: en

# Erlangen - Admin

University setup for your first week

This is not a complete arrival checklist. Address registration, health-insurance status and, where required, residence permission are separate tasks.

### 1\. Register your [Erlangen address](https://erlangen.de/service/365)

You must register within two weeks of moving in. Bring your ID or passport, your landlord's confirmation (Wohnungsgeberbestätigung) and the registration form. Late registration can cost a fine of up to €1,000.

Online registration needs an ID card with online function and is currently open to German citizens and EU citizens with an eID; non-EU residence permits are still planned. For a visit to the Rathaus (Rathausplatz 1), [book an appointment online](https://erlangen.flexappoint.de/).

### 2\. For [FAU](https://www.fau.de/studium/studienorganisation/studierendenangelegenheiten/faucard/) students: get your FAUcard

The FAUcard is free. It is your student ID, library card, e-wallet, copy card and door opener. It arrives by post after enrolment, once your IdM account exists.

From the second semester, revalidate it after each re-registration at a validation station, for example in the Kollegienhaus, Universitätsstraße 15. It takes about 30 seconds.

### 3\. For FAU students: use the Mensa

Top up your FAUcard at a machine in any [Studierendenwerk](https://www.werkswelt.de/index.php?id=kartensystem) dining hall or cafeteria, then pay with the card.

### 4\. For FAU students: buy the discounted Deutschlandticket

Erlangen has no semester ticket any more. [FAU](https://www.fau.de/studium/studentisches-leben/studierendenmobilitaet/) points students to the discounted Deutschlandticket from [VGN](https://www.vgn.de/ermaessigungsticket-studi): €43 per calendar month, valid for local and regional transport across Germany. Buy it in the VGN online shop or apps. It is delivered after processing, so it is not instant.

-   It does not cover first class, IC/ICE trains, long-distance buses, dogs or bikes. Carry an ID document.
-   The FAUcard is not a ticket. The VGN area covers Erlangen, Nuremberg and Fürth, so the same ticket serves FAU sites in all three.
-   You can cancel it monthly.

Local sources checked 22 October 2026. Check the linked pages for current prices and rules.

---

Source: https://germandex.com/erlangen/admin

Language: en


# Erlangen - Sports

## For FAU students: Hochschulsport

[FAU Hochschulsport](https://www.hochschulsport.fau.de/startseite/) runs more than 150 courses each semester, from team sports to fitness, outdoor and relaxation.

Registration is online only and opens about 7 days before courses start. Use your @fau.de email address and have your IBAN ready; the bank must take part in SEPA.

Every course has a fee. Students pay the lowest rate, plus a €2 administration fee per participation. See the [participation rules](https://www.hochschulsport.fau.de/teilnahmeinformationen/).

### Browse the [course list](https://www.hochschulsport.fau.de/kurse-classes/)

Booking is limited: usually at most three offers per category and five in total per person. The site is being redesigned; if a page looks broken, use the Courses menu.

Local sources checked 22 October 2026. Check the linked pages for current prices and rules.

---

Source: https://germandex.com/erlangen/sports

# Erlangen - Housing in Erlangen

Find a room. Know what you are signing.

### Start with Studierendenwerk Erlangen-Nürnberg

You can only apply online. The Studierendenwerk lists more than 3,600 places, from single rooms to family flats, and a free private-room service for Erlangen and Nuremberg. The search is hardest in the weeks before the winter semester, especially for international students and late admissions.

[Studierendenwerk Erlangen-Nürnberg housing](https://werkswelt.de/index.php?id=wohnen)

A residence application is not a booking. Compare shared-flat rooms and private rentals while you wait. Check the address, the landlord or main tenant, the total monthly cost and the contract before paying.

# Erlangen - Medical help in Erlangen

The right help, without guessing where to go.

### Find a doctor near you

Use the 116117 doctor search with Erlangen or your postcode. Start with a Hausarzt for general care; check the practice's contact details and ask about appointments and your insurance before going.

[Find a doctor in Erlangen](https://arztsuche.116117.de/)

## Urgent or out of hours?

During office hours, contact a Hausarzt (general practitioner). A local Apotheke (pharmacy) can advise on medicines. For urgent illness that cannot wait until the practice reopens but is not life-threatening, call 116117. For life-threatening emergencies or possible lasting harm, call 112. When unsure whether life is at risk, call 112.

[Medical help and emergency numbers](https://gesund.bund.de/notfallnummern)

## Hospital emergency departments

Uniklinikum Erlangen lists emergency departments round the clock: surgery at Krankenhausstr. 12 (entrance at Maximiliansplatz), tel. 09131 85-33260; internal medicine at Ulmenweg 18, tel. 09131 85-35420; children at Loschgestr. 15, tel. 09131 85-33118. For life-threatening emergencies call 112.

[Uniklinikum Erlangen emergency departments](https://www.uk-erlangen.de/944/)

## Pharmacies in Erlangen

Use the emergency-pharmacy search with your Erlangen address or postcode. The duty rota changes; check the current result before travelling.

[Find an emergency pharmacy](https://www.aponet.de/notdienstsuche/-)

Local sources checked 22 October 2026. Practice search results are not confirmed appointments.

---

Source: https://germandex.com/erlangen/medical

Language: en


# Tübingen - Admin

University setup for your first week

This is not a complete arrival checklist. Address registration, health-insurance status and, where required, residence permission are separate tasks.

### 1\. Register your [Tübingen address](https://www.tuebingen.de/verwaltung/verfahren/anmeldung_wohnsitz)

You must register within two weeks of moving in. It is free. Bring your ID or passport and your landlord's confirmation (Wohnungsgeberbescheinigung). Late registration is an offence and can be fined.

You can register online with an ID card with online function. In person, the Bürgerbüro (Schmiedtorstraße 4) works by appointment only; [book online](https://www.tuebingen.de/dienststellen).

### 2\. For [University of Tübingen](https://uni-tuebingen.de/studium/studienorganisation/administration/chipkarte/) students: get your student card

The Studierendensekretariat posts your chip card after enrolment. It is your student ID, opens some buildings and pays at the Mensa and at copiers.

After each re-registration, update the semester print at a self-service terminal. A lost card costs €15 to replace and unused credit is not refunded.

### 3\. For students: use the Mensa

Pay with your student card or a Mensakarte at [Studierendenwerk](https://www.my-stuwe.de/mensa/bezahlung/) dining halls and cafeterias. Autoload is optional; you can also top up at the machines on campus.

### 4\. For University of Tübingen students: buy the [naldo semester ticket](https://www.naldo.de/tickets/semesterticket/)

The semester ticket covers the whole naldo network and is sold only for the full semester. Buy it in the naldo Studi-Web-Shop after you have enrolled or re-registered. It comes as a mobile ticket with a Print@Home copy, works only with your current student ID and cannot be transferred.

-   naldo's tariff table, valid from 1 October 2025, lists €161.10 per semester. The [university page](https://uni-tuebingen.de/studium/rund-ums-studium/semesterticket/) still shows an older price, so confirm the current price in the shop.
-   Without a ticket, your student ID is valid on naldo buses and trains Monday to Friday from 19:00 and all day at weekends and on Baden-Württemberg public holidays. The university page notes a transition rule; check it.

Local sources checked 22 October 2026. Check the linked pages for current prices and rules.

---

Source: https://germandex.com/tuebingen/admin

Language: en

# Münster - Admin

University setup for your first week

This is not a complete arrival checklist. Address registration, health-insurance status and, where required, residence permission are separate tasks.

### 1\. Get a bike

The bike ("Leeze" in Münster) is the main way to get around. The city is built for it.

### 2\. Pay at the Mensa without cash

The Mensas are cashless. Pay with your student card, a MensaCard or your bank card.

Payment failed? Try another checkout or ask staff.

### 3\. For University of [Münster](https://www.uni-muenster.de/studium/orga/studienverwaltung/selfservice.html) students: download your semester ticket

At the University of Münster you get it in the SelfService portal. It covers all local and regional buses and trains in Germany.

No ticket in SelfService? Check re-registration and semester fee, then contact student administration.

-   The Deutschlandsemesterticket covers local and regional transport in second class, not ICE/IC/EC. It is funded through the semester fee, not a free ticket.
-   Do not board without a valid ticket. If your semester ticket is not ready, buy another valid fare first.

## More than university setup

### Register your Münster address

Address registration: [city registration office (Anmeldung)](https://www.stadt-muenster.de/buergerservice/meldeangelegenheiten/anmeldung), within two weeks of moving in. Residence permits: [immigration authority](https://www.stadt-muenster.de/aufenthaltsrecht/studium-und-promotion/waehrend-des-studiums). Documents, health insurance, residence status and official letters: [Germany-wide admin guide](https://germandex.com/germany/admin).

You can register [fully online](https://www.stadt-muenster.de/buergerservice/meldeangelegenheiten/anmeldung) (your ID chip is updated and the address sticker arrives by post) or in person with an appointment at a Bürgerbüro or Bezirksverwaltung.

---

Source: https://germandex.com/muenster/admin

Language: en

Deposits, running costs, move-in confirmation and scam checks: read the [housing guide for Germany](https://germandex.com/germany/housing) before signing.

Local source checked 1 October 2026. Check the provider for current eligibility and availability.

# Düsseldorf - Medical help in Düsseldorf

The right help, without guessing where to go.

### Find a doctor near you

Use KV Nordrhein's practice search with Düsseldorf or your postcode. Start with a Hausarzt for general medical care; check the practice's contact details and ask about appointments and your insurance before going.

[Find a doctor in Düsseldorf](https://patienten.kvno.de/praxissuche)

## Urgent or out of hours?

During office hours, contact a Hausarzt (general practitioner). A local Apotheke (pharmacy) can advise on medicines. For urgent illness that cannot wait until the practice reopens but is not life-threatening, call 116117. For life-threatening emergencies or possible lasting harm, call 112. When unsure whether life is at risk, call 112.

[Medical help and emergency numbers](https://gesund.bund.de/notfallnummern)

## Pharmacies in Düsseldorf

Use the emergency-pharmacy search with your Düsseldorf address or postcode. The duty rota changes; check the current result before travelling.

[Find an emergency pharmacy](https://www.aponet.de/notdienstsuche/-)

Local lookup source checked 1 October 2026. Practice search results are not confirmed appointments.

---

Source: https://germandex.com/duesseldorf/medical

# Hamburg - Housing in Hamburg

Find a room. Know what you are signing.

### Start with Studierendenwerk Hamburg

You can choose up to three houses or apply for all houses. The provider says applying for all houses improves your chances. Reply to its regular interest-confirmation emails by the stated deadline to stay on the list.

[Studierendenwerk Hamburg housing](https://www.stwhh.de/wohnen/bewerbungsinformationen)

# Cologne - Housing in Cologne

Find a room. Know what you are signing.

### Start with Kölner Studierendenwerk

Apply online early. You can specify room type, move-in date and budget, but not a particular residence. Confirm the interest-check email within five days; otherwise the application is deactivated.

[Kölner Studierendenwerk housing](https://www.kstw.de/wohnen/bewerbung/)

## Keep a second search running

# Münster - Housing in Münster

Find a room. Know what you are signing.

### Start with Studierendenwerk Münster

New students can apply without an admission letter. Choose up to three residences carefully: the choice cannot later be changed. Watch for email offers and reply; ignoring an offer can delete your application.

[Studierendenwerk Münster housing](https://www.stw-muenster.de/wohnen/bewerbung-wohnraum/)

## Keep a second search running

A residence application is not a booking. Compare shared-flat rooms and private rentals in Münster while you wait. Check the address, the landlord or main tenant, the total monthly cost and the contract before paying.
